title: Breakfast at Tiffany's
tagline: Grace in every frame, humanity in every cause.

scenes.text: Hollywood, 1953. A twenty-four year old Belgian actress arrives from the London stage. Her face is unlike any Hollywood had seen — all cheekbones and enormous dark eyes. Within a year she will win an Oscar, a Tony, and change what beauty means to an entire generation.

scenes.speaker: Audrey Hepburn
scenes.text: I was a war child. I was hungry — truly hungry, as a child in occupied Netherlands. That changes you. I cannot look at abundance without thinking of those who have none. Which is why, in the end, UNICEF matters more to me than cinema.

challenge.fact: Audrey Hepburn won an Oscar (Roman Holiday, 1953), Tony (Ondine, 1954), Emmy (Love Among Thieves, 1993), and Grammy (spoken word album, 1993) — becoming one of very few EGOT winners. She also received the Presidential Medal of Freedom.

scenes.text: In her final years, Hepburn served as a UNICEF Goodwill Ambassador, traveling to Somalia, Ethiopia, Sudan, and Bangladesh — places far from Hollywood's lights. She called her humanitarian work her greatest role.

challenge.instruction: Arrange the opening notes of 'Moon River' — the song Audrey Hepburn sang in Breakfast at Tiffany's.
challenge.fact: 'Moon River' won the 1962 Academy Award for Best Original Song. When Paramount executives suggested cutting it, Hepburn reportedly said: 'Over my dead body!' Henry Mancini's melody became her signature.

scenes.speaker: Audrey Hepburn
scenes.text: I believe in pink. I believe that laughing is the best calorie burner. I believe in kissing, kissing a lot. I believe in being strong when everything seems to be going wrong. I believe that happy girls are the prettiest girls.

challenge.fact: Hepburn won the Oscar, Tony, Emmy, and Grammy — one of very few EGOT recipients. But she considered her UNICEF work her greatest achievement, visiting famine-stricken communities in Ethiopia, Sudan, Bangladesh, and Central America in her final years.

challenge.fact: Hepburn won the Oscar for Roman Holiday (1953), her film debut. For Breakfast at Tiffany's (1961), she received a nomination but lost to Sophia Loren. The film's song "Moon River" won the Oscar for Best Original Song — Henry Mancini wrote it specifically for Hepburn's vocal range.

Audrey Hepburn loved the Louvre. Reassemble da Vinci's Mona Lisa — swap tiles until her enigmatic smile is whole again.
challenge.fact: Da Vinci worked on the Mona Lisa from approximately 1503 to 1517, carrying it with him when he moved to France. X-ray scans reveal three entirely different compositions beneath the final paint.

challenge.instruction: Four wings of the Louvre await your curatorial eye. Place each masterpiece in the room that earns the greatest bonus and open the museum doors.
challenge.fact: Audrey Hepburn was a devoted visitor of European museums and served as a UNICEF ambassador for the last five years of her life, championing education and the arts for children worldwide.
